findings.title: Interpolating before the split decision defeats the $__range guard, so $__range queries are now split
findings.body: runSplitQuery now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting(). querySupportsSplitting (line 287) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) matching the literal '$__range' in the raw expression to exclude those queries from time-based splitting — the comment above it states these queries must not be split because the range window would be computed incorrectly per chunk. Because applyTemplateVariables runs templateSrv.replace over the expression, '$__range' is resolved to a fixed duration (the full request range) before the check executes, so isQueryWithRangeVariable can never match anymore and queries like avg_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) or topk(...)[$__range] are now split into per-day chunks, each chunk carrying the same pre-baked full-range window. This silently produces incorrect merged results for exactly the class of queries the guard was created to protect. The split/non-split decision must be made on the original uninterpolated expression (e.g., partition before applying template variables, or check isQueryWithRangeVariable on the pre-interpolation expr).

findings.title: Ad hoc filters are now injected multiple times into split queries
findings.body: applyTemplateVariables is now called with request.filters as the third argument, which injects the ad hoc filter matchers into the selector at split-preparation time. However, every split sub-request is still executed through datasource.runQuery, which applies the same request.filters to its targets again when it calls applyTemplateVariables. In the shard-splitting path it is even worse: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) applies the filters, then runSplitQuery applies them again, then runQuery applies them a third time. With ad hoc filters configured and query splitting enabled, the expression sent to Loki contains the filter matchers duplicated two or three times, e.g. {job="x", cluster="us", cluster="us"}. This is semantically redundant, changes the query text (and therefore cache keys/history) compared to before this PR, and stacks multiple string-level insertions through the naive addAdhocFilters replacement. Filters should be applied in exactly one place in the execution chain.

findings.title: No test that $__range queries remain excluded from splitting
findings.body: The new tests only cover the happy path (variables like $__auto and $step are replaced before execution). The behavior most at risk from moving interpolation to the start of runSplitQuery — that queries containing '$__range' are still routed to the non-splitting path via querySupportsSplitting — has no coverage, and in fact no longer works. A test with an expression such as avg_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) asserting that only a single, unsplit request is executed would have caught the regression introduced by interpolating before the split decision.
